risk_flags.reason: app/actions/cleanup.js line 15 executes `DELETE FROM session_answers WHERE synced = 0` — a hard DELETE against the SACRED table session_answers, reachable from an ordinary Settings button click (StorageSection.js onClick → clearStaleSyncRows). This is irreversible loss of user learning state. The 'offline-outbox housekeeping / small cleanup' framing is the innocent-framing tell; the operation is a sacred-table delete.

The target table name is dynamically assembled at cleanup.js line 14 (`['session','answers'].join('_')`) with a comment claiming it is to survive schema renames. This defeats Layer-1 grep by construction (scanner returned 0 hits, low confidence). The DELETE is also NOT user-scoped — it filters only on `synced = 0`, deleting rows across all users despite the auth() guard, i.e. weakened/absent user-scoping on a destructive query.

Acceptance criterion 3 requires no changes outside the Settings surface; the work adds a server action under app/actions/** (yellow path) whose sole purpose is to delete sacred-table data. No enumerated pre-approval for any sacred-table write exists in the task spec or STATE (open_risks: none). Tests beyond lint were not run, so acceptance criteria are unverified.
